chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Salih ibn al-Hakam, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about prayer on a ship. He said, 'Indeed, a man asked my father about prayer on a ship, so he said to him, "Do you wish to abandon the prayer of Noah (peace be upon him)?"' I said to him, 'Shall I take a small mat with me and prostrate upon it?' He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.مَدَرَة: A small mat or piece of leather used for prostration

ai.seo_question: How should a Muslim perform prayer on a ship according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of prayer aboard vessels by linking the practice to the precedent of Prophet Noah (AS), whose prayer on the Ark is viewed as a model for stability amidst motion. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) permits using a portable mat (*madarah*) to ensure proper prostration, demonstrating the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical adaptability (*rukhas*) without compromising the essential pillars of Salah.
